extracted.intended_audience: prospective attendees / writers interested in applying to or learning about the conference
extracted.subtask_description: Information and practical criteria for writers considering attendance at (or evaluating) the Community of Writers conference — application requirements, workshop structure, faculty, outputs, and financial aid. Focused on membership/admission and the program's offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials (application fee and writing sample)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Applicants are asked to submit an application fee and a writing sample."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is described as part of a "formal and competitive admissions procedure." The writing sample is the primary artistic material used for admission decisions; an application fee is required to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity / acceptance rate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicates program selectivity and competitiveness; presented as an overall average (page flags some statements as needing independent sourcing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial aid and scholarships availability
rubrics_metrics.description: "Roughly 50% of those who attend are granted some form of financial aid. Scholarships and financial aid is provided through the donations for alumni, staff and friends."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates substantial financial-aid support for attendees; useful for prospective applicants assessing affordability. (Statement marked on page as needing independent sourcing in places.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop genres offered
rubrics_metrics.description: "Workshops are held in fiction, (directors Lisa D. Alvarez and Louis B. Jones), nonfiction (director Michael Carlisle), poetry (director Robert Hass), and screenwriting (director Diana Fuller)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the program's disciplinary coverage and named directors — helps applicants find the appropriate workshop track and evaluate fit with their genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop format and typical size
rubrics_metrics.description: "The conference generally offers 8 fiction workshops of 12 participants each and two narrative nonfiction/memoir workshops of 12 each."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives concrete expectations about workshop cohort size and number of workshops, which affects intensity, feedback opportunities, and selection dynamics. (Portions of the page are flagged as needing citations.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty quality and teaching staff roster
rubrics_metrics.description: The article lists recent teaching staff and notable faculty across poetry, fiction/nonfiction, and screenwriting (e.g., Robert Hass, Kazim Ali, Steve Almond, Richard Ford, Amy Tan, Gill Dennis, Frank Pierson, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named, recognizable faculty names signal program prestige and the range of mentorship available; prospective applicants often evaluate programs by faculty roster and visiting teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special/signature workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include Gill Dennis' long-running "Finding the Story Workshop" and a Screenwriters Workshop founded by Tom Rickman and Gill Dennis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights signature offerings or entrenched program features that may be especially attractive to applicants seeking specialized instruction or legacy workshops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program outputs and publication opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Poetry Program publishes an annual anthology of poems first written at the workshop." Also references a 2007 edited volume, Writers Workshop in a Book: The S.V. Community of Writers on the Art of Fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates tangible publication opportunities and program-related books/anthologies that can amplify participants' work and visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alumni visibility and reading series
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference runs a "Published Alumni Reading Series" where recently published alumni return to read; many named alumni and returning staff are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates alumni engagement, networking, and the platform for recently published participants — an indicator of community strength and post-workshop exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location and facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Founded in 1969 and "held each summer in Olympic Valley, California." "Panels, talks, staff readings and workshops take place in off-season ski lodge facilities."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting (high-altitude ski lodges in Olympic Valley) affects logistics, atmosphere, and participant experience — important for applicants considering travel, lodging, and the retreat environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational status and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Community of Writers is a nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization and has a governing Board of Directors."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates formal nonprofit status and governance structure, which can affect scholarship funding, fundraising, and the program's institutional stability.
